better_overall.reason: A is the more polished, welcoming and complete site, and its booking is more capable: it offers the next three Saturdays, handles the day itself, falls back to copying the booking if no email app opens, and can be connected to a form service. Its honesty problems are placeholder details the organiser has to swap for real ones anyway (the made-up phone number and address need replacing first). B's honesty, simplicity and ticket idea do not quite make up for its thinner content and weaker visual finish.

post_code_notes: The code does not change my stage-1 verdicts, and B's ticket idea goes further than the screenshots show. In B, the selected slot turns magenta, and submitting builds a large 'Your ticket' summary with a stub, plus 'Email your ticket' and 'Copy ticket text' buttons and a candid 'This is not a booking yet' line. Errors use a GOV.UK-style summary at the top as well as messages next to each field, and the page title changes when there is a problem. The example address is flagged only to visitors who reach the ticket. Weak points in B: only the next session can be booked, and without JavaScript the page shows a fixed 'Saturday 3 October' (2026-10-03), which will go out of date. In A, the date and the 'Tomorrow' pill are worked out from today's date (it also says 'today' or 'on now'), and without JavaScript it shows 'First Saturday of every month'. A also offers the next three Saturdays, swaps a booking on the day itself for a 'just drop in' message, opens a pre-filled email and then shows a done panel with a copy fallback and 'Book another item', and has an optional form-service setup with sent and failed states. The 'Note for the organisers' appears only while the address is still an example.* address, which softens my stage-1 concern about it. But the phone number 01632 960123 (an Ofcom number reserved for drama) and 'Church Street, Your Town AB1 2CD' with an 'Open in Maps' link are invented and not flagged. So are several stated policies, such as 'people with a slot are seen first', 'one item per booking', 'Later slots are usually quieter' and 'no volunteers for phones yet'. Neither site can limit bookings per slot, because there is no backend; both rely on a volunteer replying to confirm.
